title: Fine
subtitle: Strength includes asking for help
sourceCredit: Fred Johnson · The Moth, “A Hard Truth”

shot.title: At attention
shot.direction: Hold a rigid upright body beneath the small FINE bubble. The space around him feels too orderly.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

illustration.direction: In a quiet orderly room, the soldier stands unnaturally straight beside a plain wooden chair, heels grounded and hands held too tightly together. Small medals are genuinely pinned to his olive shirt, one resting slightly askew. A compressed soft charcoal cloud above his head suggests restless nights without picturing combat or faces. His mouth is controlled, his eyes tired. The wall and floor remain ordinary, giving the rigid silhouette room to be read.

shot.title: One medal moves
shot.direction: A medal gives a tiny tremor; a night silhouette unsettles the cloud above his head.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

beats.caption: You haven’t slept again, have you?
beats.speaker: FAMILY

shot.title: Someone notices the night
shot.direction: The question comes from family offscreen. He avoids answering with his eyes.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

illustration.direction: The same man now sits on the edge of the home chair, feet flat, back still military straight, fingers interlocked over his knees. He glances away toward a dim doorway where the family voice comes from; no other person is shown. One shoulder has drawn defensively inward. The charcoal pressure shape has crowded closer to him, but there are no literal monsters or war scenes. His reassurance looks practiced and exhausting.

shot.title: The familiar armor
shot.direction: He repeats the familiar reassurance as the cloud crowds his silhouette.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

shot.title: The second chair
shot.direction: Reveal the therapist in an ordinary second chair. Allow the scene to become human in scale.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

illustration.direction: A modest consultation room with two real chairs placed at an open angle and a low table with water, no barrier desk. The soldier sits braced in one chair; the therapist sits opposite at equal eye height, feet on the same floor and hands resting on her own lap. She leans only slightly forward and asks gently, leaving his personal space intact. His medals and clenched hands remain visible; the setting is human rather than clinical spectacle.

beats.caption: And what has carrying it cost you?
beats.speaker: THERAPIST

shot.title: The cost of carrying
shot.direction: The therapist asks without leaning into his space. His fingers release one another.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

shot.title: The shoulders lower
shot.direction: He sits. The shoulder line slowly softens and his hands stop bracing the chair.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

illustration.direction: From a closer but still complete two-chair view, the soldier eases back enough that the chair actually supports his weight. His hands have unlinked, one palm resting on his thigh and the other releasing the chair arm. His shoulders lower unevenly and his eyes turn down. The therapist remains quietly present with her own hands still. The compressed graphite cloud has a small opening, not a vanishing cure. Keep chair legs and both people's grounded feet coherent.

actions.direction: The shoulders soften before the chin dips. Both seated hands and the chair arms remain grounded; no sudden collapse or oscillating distress.

beats.caption: I don’t think I know how to put it down.
beats.speaker: SOLDIER

shot.title: An admission
shot.direction: His gaze drops, then returns. Allow the full admission and the silence following it.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

illustration.direction: The soldier lifts his gaze toward the therapist with a vulnerable, searching expression, one hand turned a little upward near his knee rather than gesturing grandly. His other hand rests loosely. She receives the admission with a calm face and no consoling touch that he has not invited. The same chairs and small table fix their distance. Soft warm light reaches his face while the medals remain pinned and the night-colored cloud remains faintly present.

actions.direction: The seated soldier leans a fraction toward the listener; his open palm follows the breath, holds the admission, then lowers. The listener answers with one small attentive inclination.

beats.caption: You don’t have to learn that part alone.
beats.speaker: THERAPIST

shot.title: Room to learn
shot.direction: The reply does not solve the memories. The edge of the constricting bubble opens.
shot.soundDirection: A marching drum pulse gradually replaced by breathing and soft room ambience.

illustration.direction: Widen slightly to both seated people sharing an ordinary breathing space. The therapist offers one small open hand over her own knee as she replies; the soldier's relaxed hands and newly level shoulders show he can hear her. The cloud's edge is open to room light, but its graphite traces and the small medals are still there. No triumphant transformation, embrace or suddenly carefree grin; simply two bodies supported by their chairs.

shot.title: Breathing space
shot.direction: Hold two seated people and an ordinary breath. The medals and memories are not erased.
